review_scope: Registered-source review of Change acceleration and detection by Yanglei Song and Georgios Fellouris. The fixed 53-page PDF is arXiv:1710.00915v5, dated 21 June 2024. Main text and references extend through the top of page 26, clipped above y=137.4. A separate narrow crop contains only the Appendix A heading; all appendix bodies are excluded.
inventory: Three main-text Theorems: 3.1 on page 8, 5.1 on pages 12-13 and 6.1 on page 17. Complete statements were compared with their rendered source pages. Fresh uppercase-heading enumeration over all permitted pages distinguishes the actual environments from the ordinary-case mention on page 16, proof references, Lemmas and Corollaries.
original_statements: Theorem 3.1 retains the Markovian condition (1), the specific optimal procedure (9), the auxiliary optimization (6), arbitrary positive cost c, the boundary function from R^kappa to R_+, the stopping threshold in posterior odds and the zero-dimensional memoryless special case. Blackboard-bold S is retained for its sufficient statistic.

Theorem 5.1 retains conditions (14) and (16), arbitrary block lengths, epsilon>0, b2>=b1>1 and d>1. Its leading expectation inequality, eta formula and every term of U are complete. The page-13 continuation includes both M terms, 3ell1+2ell2, all three variance ratios, the log-zeta term and the complete optional initial-prefix extension (21), including its constant and both survival sums.

Theorem 6.1 retains response condition (14), change-model conditions (27) and (28), condition (29), the infimum over C_alpha and the multiplicative asymptotic lower bound involving lambda-star and |log(alpha)|/D-star. The Section 6 ratio convention is archived separately without changing the original theorem.
source_passages: All 31 source passages and six auxiliary excerpts were compared with the rendered main text. The latent absorbing change, observed filtration and prior/conditional hazard preserve the distinction between latent and observable history. Policies remain deterministic and predictable with a deterministic first treatment. Response densities live on the common Polish space and retain the full conditional-independence statement.

General treatment-history hazards, policy-dependent Theta, Markov sufficient-state link/update and memoryless specialization match pages 4-5. Fixed-dimensional Markov state does not become a finite-memory restriction. The admissible class and its false-alarm-constrained subclass remain distinct.

Posterior odds and the main-text recursion, known-model convention, auxiliary sample-size-plus-false-alarm objective, controlled state/action dynamics, delayed termination flag, nonnegative stage cost, infinite-horizon value, action-specific and Bellman operators and optimal procedure match pages 6-8. The predictive density phi is explicitly referred to Appendix B.1 (B.1); its unavailable formula remains unresolved.

The treatment blocks, periodic indexing and slices, likelihood ratio, posterior/likelihood crossing times, full alternating assignment, recursive stage endpoints, detection-favoring tie rule and finite initial-prefix extension match pages 9-11. Sigma allows zero additional observations whereas tau starts at one; plain stage-endpoint S is distinct from the Markov state.

Directional KL information numbers, centered likelihood variances, full uniform stability quantifiers, omega transform, block averages, adjusted information, initial expected change time, worst-history residual bound and uniform two-block maximal-hazard lower bound match pages 11-12. Only the initial expectation carries 1-pi0. The switching threshold d is distinct from d(Xi).

The alpha-indexed family and ratio conventions match page 16; response densities remain fixed. Conditions (27)-(29) match page 17, including the uniform upper hazard bound, existence of a residual-duration block, infimum defining lambda-star, positive bounded D-star, the floor window and uniformity over times and policies. The original D-star naming context on page 18 is retained.
dependency_review: All 25 direct uses, 45 related connections and 31 local dependency lists were checked. Theorem 3.1 uses Markov control and the unconstrained objective, without the proposed block algorithm, response variance condition or alpha-family. Theorem 5.1 uses the general change model and cyclic procedure, without Markov optimality or later optimized thresholds and block designs. Theorem 6.1 uses all admissible procedures and the existence condition on residual time; it does not inherit cyclic assignment, Markov structure, condition (16), block-adjusted information or optimal-design assumptions. The scalar omega definition is archived independently so that its reuse does not import the surrounding stability condition.
names_and_highlights: All source-derived natural-language names, source kinds and labels were checked. Every interface has a selector identifying its own source passage or label, all additional selectors occur in related same-paper statements, and relationship explanations follow actual local paths. Naming evidence for likelihood ratio is on page 9 and fastest speed on page 18. Font checks distinguish blackboard-bold S, plain stage S, sans-serif D/E and script R.
source_limitations: All 33 existing notes are preserved, including source version and appendix boundary; two-page theorem completeness; notation distinctions; unobserved latent history; deterministic policies; possible zero hazards and posterior denominators; fixed-dimensional versus finite memory; delayed stopping flag; appendix-only phi; missing measurability/version and tie-selection details; total-sample-cost objective; hitting-time boundary cases and reset conventions; first-stage-only prefix; centered moments and their unequal positivity requirements; uniform stability; unoptimized thresholds; conditional residual-time wording; possible zero zeta/infinite bounds; alpha-ratio semantics; prior inclusion in (27); existence rather than universal block restriction; the printed epsilon>0 range versus nonpositive windows for epsilon>=1; and the unspecified interpretation of random-history suprema. No repairs or proof certification are claimed.
